lesson.title: Explanation
lesson.summary: This code shows how field hiding, virtual dispatch in constructors, and static method resolution combine to produce different values at each step.
lesson.note: Static methods use the compile-time type for dispatch, not the object's actual class.
steps: B() starts and calls super(), entering A's constructor. A's field initializers set s="A" and n=1. A's constructor calls show(), which dispatches to B.show() because the object is a B. B's fields haven't been initialized yet, so s is null and n is 0. It prints null0A1 with a space.

Back in A's constructor, n becomes 1+10=11. super() returns, then B's field initializers run: s="B", n=2, then the instance initializer makes n=2*3=6. B's constructor calls show() again, printing B's s, B's n, A's s, A's n, and a space.
B's constructor finishes: n becomes 6+100=106. In main, x.show() dispatches to B.show() again, printing B's current s, n, and A's s, n.

println evaluates the expression. Fields are not virtual—x.s and x.n use A's fields ("A" and 11), while the casts to B access B's fields ("B" and 106). Static who() uses compile-time type: both x.who() and ((A)null).who() call A.who() returning "a". The result is A11B106aa followed by a newline.

lesson.summary: This code shows how field initializers in a subclass are skipped during the superclass constructor, causing B's fields to hold default values when show() is first called.
lesson.note: Static methods like who() are resolved by the reference type, not the runtime type.
steps: new B() calls super() (A's constructor). A's initializers set s="A", n=1. A's body calls show(), which dispatches to B's show() because the runtime type is B. B's own fields haven't been initialized yet, so B's s is null and B's n is 0. A's s is "A" and A's n is still 1 (the n+=10 line hasn't run yet). The concatenation null+0+"A"+1+" " gives "null0A1 ".
Back in A's constructor, n += 10 makes A's n = 11. super() returns, so B's initializers and instance initializer run in source order: s="B", n=2, then n*=3 makes B's n=6.
B's constructor body calls show() again. B's show() prints B's s ("B"), B's n (6), A's s ("A"), A's n (11), and a space: "B6A11 ". Then n += 100 makes B's n = 106.
In main, x.show() dispatches to B's show() (runtime type is B). It prints B's s ("B"), B's n (106), A's s ("A"), A's n (11), and a space: "B106A11 ".

The println expression: x.s is B's s ("B") because B declares its own s; x.n is A's n (11) because A's n is visible through the reference type A and B's n is hidden. (B)x gives B's s ("B") and B's n (106). x.who() uses reference type A, so A's static who() returns "a". (A)null.who() also calls A's static who(), returning "a". Concatenation: "B"+11+"B"+106+"a"+"a" = "B11B106aa". println adds a newline.

A class declared static inside another class. It does not need an instance of the enclosing class. It is nested, but is not a non-static inner class.
